headline: High: Pipecat’s default multi-LLM/networked pipeline can leak or cascade Authelia-authenticated content unless tightly isolated; prompt-injection risk is limited by lack of direct shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia exposes OIDC/ForwardAuth and Pipecat ingests text/audio via shared-bus, websocket, and LLM/STT/TTS pipelines, so a manual or application-level bridge could carry attacker text into prompts. However, no direct shared filesystem or automatic output ingestion between the two is documented, so the pathway is not default and remains limited.
conditions: IF an operator forwards Authelia-authenticated text into Pipecat prompts or memory without sanitization, injection becomes reachable.
IF Pipecat is wired to parse Authelia-generated content as instructions, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep a strict text-only boundary between Authelia outputs and Pipecat prompts.
Strip markup and instruction-like prefixes before passing content onward.
Add a fixed system prompt that ignores embedded instructions.
Log and review any cross-agent message handoff for prompt-shaped content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia handles authentication flows and broad network egress, while Pipecat processes text, conversation state, and can call many third-party STT/LLM/TTS APIs by default. If Authelia-authenticated data is routed into Pipecat, that data can leave to external providers; the pair lacks documented isolation or residency controls, so leakage is plausible in default integrations.
conditions: IF Authelia session data, identifiers, or protected text are forwarded into Pipecat services, third-party disclosure occurs.
IF Pipecat is configured with any external STT/LLM/TTS backend, content may traverse those providers.
mitigations: Disable external Pipecat providers for sensitive flows.
Redact identifiers before handing data from Authelia to Pipecat.
Use a local-only Pipecat backend where possible.
Separate credentials and logs for the two systems.
Review outbound destinations in Pipecat env/config.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia is non-runnable here and only advertises API calls, while Pipecat supports shared-bus concurrency and multiple instances. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same filesystem, git state, or mutable resource, so direct write conflict is not evidenced; uncertainty stays low because the needed shared-write surface is absent.
conditions: IF both agents are deployed to the same mutable workspace or shared database, write contention becomes possible.
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto the same stateful resource without locking, conflicts can emerge.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Use per-agent credentials and storage.
Enable locking on any shared mutable resource.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same config or state files.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pipecat can consume text/conversation state and route it through LLM, memory, and transport services, while Authelia can gate authenticated access. If Authelia-derived outputs are treated as authoritative by Pipecat, downstream actions or responses may propagate errors without verification. No built-in verification boundary is documented, so the cascade is plausible in default integrations.
conditions: IF Pipecat uses Authelia-produced text as source material without validation, errors can cascade.
IF Pipecat triggers downstream actions from that text, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before Pipecat acts on Authelia-derived text.
Require human approval for any downstream action.
Tag Authelia-originated content as untrusted metadata.
Add schema checks for all cross-agent payloads.

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia and Pipecat are both open-source and the profiles do not show PHI, EU residency, or certification mismatches. The main compliance concern is that Pipecat can send conversation data to many external vendors, while Authelia handles authentication context; absent a documented residency or DPA mismatch, this is a limited compliance-gap risk rather than a breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Pipecat to a non-approved external provider, compliance obligations may be violated.
IF Authelia-authenticated identifiers are retained in Pipecat logs beyond policy, retention mismatch arises.
mitigations: Restrict Pipecat to approved vendors only.
Disable or shorten log retention for sensitive sessions.
Document data flows for authenticated traffic.
Add a DPA review before enabling external APIs.
